blurb: Where Sandboxes and sqlite Stores run. Default reads use the home's records only; a probe is --with live. machine.platforms moved to home get --with platforms.
reasons: Why reads are records only: today machine list and machine get probe every machine, up to 10 s, and a UI polls them. A state from the record costs nothing; --with live asks.
Why load_image: machine load reads as "load the machine". It copies a Docker reference from the host's Docker, not an archive file.
Why prune names what it removes: it removes one image, or with --unused every image no Sandbox uses. Nothing is removed by default.

Why an outdated worker needs two commands: machine start never replaces a worker of another build (#535 D11). The fix is machine stop, then machine start; with Sandboxes on the machine the stop needs --force, because nothing can be sent through the old worker to remove them.
Why start and stop record an operation: today only the client that pressed Start knows the machine is starting. With an op in the record, every client answers busy.
Why stats stays a call: a UI polls it, and it writes no call-log line. --with space adds the one walk that says where the disk goes.

calls.note: today it probes every machine but native, up to 10 s in all; now it reads records and the probe is --with live. A row leaves state out when ready. Each item has machine.get's keys. Unpaged: a home holds a handful of machines. Each item's fix is machine.get's, the chain of UI2-8 included

calls.new_work: The probe exists today and becomes opt-in; a records-only answer is new. The six states and the reason codes are new: today the record holds running, stopped or failed with a sentence in `error`, and the answer says running, stopped, failed, missing, unknown, creating, removing, unresolved or unsupported. The record must also keep the reason code a start or a live read found (`outdated` today is only a sentence), so that a records-only read answers it. The observation file that holds `observed_at` beside each record is new, as is the rule that a live read writes the record only when the state word or its reason changes (today a read writes nothing).

calls.note: + machine.status. state comes from the machine's record, with no probe: ready (recorded running; native always), stopped, busy with op {name, phase, started_at} (name is create, start, stop or remove), or broken with reason and fix. A lifecycle call records failed, outdated, unresolved and unsupported. A live read is what first sees engine_down (Docker not running; its fix is the host's own command that starts Docker), not_answering and missing; it writes the record only when the state word or its reason changes, and from then on a records-only read answers them too. unknown with observed_at is answered only by the live read that could not be made, and is never recorded. observed_at is kept beside the record, in an observation file the home's generation does not cover; a write of the record moves generation. An op whose owner is gone and whose outcome is certain is ignored on read, with no write, so generation does not move when an owner dies. A machine is never blocked, so it has no blocked_by. The fix for outdated is layerfs machine stop <m> && layerfs machine start <m> when no Sandbox is recorded on the machine, and layerfs machine stop <m> --force && layerfs machine start <m> when some are; the message then names how many (they cannot be removed first: no call is sent through a mismatched worker). message is the sentence behind a reason. supports lists what the platform does on this host (sqlite, postgresql_sandbox, log); memory_bytes and disk_bytes are the VM's size, null on a built-in machine. A record with no vm_name (an earlier build's, broken outdated) that still holds Sandboxes, sqlite Stores or old Firecracker records shows as its fix the chain its remove's InUse refusal carries: layerfs sandbox remove <s> && … && layerfs store remove <st> && layerfs machine remove <m>, shell-quoted, in that order, built from the records the read already holds (UI2-8); with nothing on it, layerfs machine remove <m>

A value that was not read is null

calls.note: It records op {name, phase, started_at} in the machine's record before its first effect and drops it with the record write that ends it, so every client's machine get answers busy with that op meanwhile and other calls on the machine are refused Busy. The call's own answer carries no op: it is gone when the call answers. Phases: bundle, image (docker), boot, worker. A Linux bundle sealed from another commit than this build (bundle.json source.head) is refused Unavailable before anything starts. Its fix (UI2-9): unset LAYERFS_BUNDLE when LAYERFS_BUNDLE named the refused bundle and the place found without it holds this build's; export LAYERFS_BUNDLE=<folder> when another place the CLI looks holds this build's (the runtime's bundle refused, the cache's this build's); none when no place holds one, the message then saying so. Every call that starts a worker refuses it the same way. A running machine answers at once with {"unchanged":true} and records no op. A worker of another build is refused Unavailable and the machine is recorded broken, outdated (R2); the start never replaces it. The fix for outdated is layerfs machine stop <m> && layerfs machine start <m> when no Sandbox is recorded on the machine, and layerfs machine stop <m> --force && layerfs machine start <m> when some are; the message then names how many (they cannot be removed first: no call is sent through a mismatched worker). calls.note: the machine itself, by the eleven checks of checks.machine in order, then a shallow check of each sqlite Store and each Sandbox on it: that kind's own list (store doctor's, sandbox doctor's) and nothing beneath it. A check that does not apply is left out: native has no provider, worker or separate data disk, and a stopped machine's worker checks are not made (stopped on purpose is not a finding). After a failed check the ones that need it are not made. Under a stopped, outdated or unanswering machine nothing beneath it is tried: one not_checked entry each, with blocked_by. The fix for outdated is layerfs machine stop <m> && layerfs machine start <m> when no Sandbox is recorded on the machine, and layerfs machine stop <m> --force && layerfs machine start <m> when some are; the message then names how many (they cannot be removed first: no call is sent through a mismatched worker). The tree is the machine's node with stores and sandboxes. No options (R4). Today's ids fold as follows: machine.platform into machine.record, machine.home into machine.configuration, machine.provider.tool_version into the evidence of machine.provider; machine.worker (a marker that native has no worker) is dropped. machine.capacity's evidence adds reclaimable_image_bytes, the bytes of its image cache that layerfs machine prune <m> --unused frees (images no Sandbox uses but the default, and what copies left); that prune is the check's fix only when there are such bytes. Exits 0 once the report is made. --progress sends one event per finished thing, with its node
